`Ping` never appears because a `.meta.json` file can't create an instance. It only changes an instance Rojo already builds from a sibling file, such as `Ping.luau` or a `Ping/` folder. Nothing in `Remotes/` produces a `Ping`, so Rojo has nothing to apply your meta file to and ignores it.

**Fix:** rename the file to `src/shared/Foo/Remotes/Ping.model.json` and keep the same content:

```json
{"className": "RemoteEvent"}
```

A `.model.json` must declare `className`, and that is what creates the instance. Rojo names it after the file, so you get `Remotes.Ping`, a RemoteEvent.

If `Remotes` also holds children you made in Studio, add `Remotes/init.meta.json` with `{"className": "Folder", "ignoreUnknownInstances": true}` so Rojo doesn't delete them on sync.

The project doesn't try to debug it. It regenerates the key, following `wiki/reference/open-cloud.md:11`:

1. Go to https://create.roblox.com/dashboard/credentials → **API Keys**.
2. Open the existing key and click **Regenerate**, or create a new key with the `asset:write` scope.
3. In `.env`, replace the old line with `ROBLOX_OPEN_CLOUD_API_KEY=<new value>`.
4. Re-run the call that failed.

The page says finding the root cause isn't worth the time. The key the dashboard gives you seems to stop working after a short time, even when it's set to never expire. So regenerate it whenever it fails, and never commit it.

Use the thumbnail URL format instead of `rbxassetid://`:

```
rbxthumb://type=Asset&id=<id>&w=420&h=420
```

A Decal uploaded through Open Cloud returns the Decal's asset id. That id doesn't resolve as an image texture through `rbxassetid://`, which is why the label stays blank. `rbxthumb://` asks Roblox for a rendered thumbnail of the asset, and that works for Decals.

For example:

```lua
imageLabel.Image = "rbxthumb://type=Asset&id=" .. decalId .. "&w=420&h=420"
```

There's more detail in `wiki/reference/open-cloud.md`.

No, the game isn't that slow. The 66.668 ms reading is exactly 1/15 s, which is Studio's frame-rate cap when its window isn't focused. A duration that lands exactly on 1/N seconds is a pacing target, not a measurement. In the same situation `RenderThreadAverage` reads about 2.4 ms. This is in `wiki/reference/roblox-engine.md:21`.

To measure render cost, count work per frame instead, since pacing and focus don't change counts:
- **`Stats.RenderBreakdown`**: its `Opaque`, `Transparent`, `UI`, `Particles` and other children return strings like `"7598 tris, 121 draws"` from `:GetValueString()`.
- **`Stats.FrameRateManager`**: `Batches`, `Indices`, `MaterialChanges`.
- **Fix the quality level** at `RenderSettings.QualityLevel = Level21`, and set it back to `Automatic` afterwards because it's a persistent Studio setting.

Report counts rather than times. `RenderThreadAverage` varies between runs about as much as most effects you'd measure.

Your `require` didn't get the game's copy of the module. Code run through `execute_luau` gets its **own copy of every ModuleScript**. So your `require(SpellRegistry)` built a fresh table, and the change went into that table. The running server and clients keep the instances they already required, so they never see it. (See `wiki/reference/studio-mcp.md`.)

To drive gameplay from injected code:

- **Set attributes the game already listens for**, on Instances such as players, characters, arena parts or `workspace`. Instances are shared across the whole DataModel, so the game's own `GetAttributeChangedSignal` handlers fire.
- **Watch results through Instances**, for example with `DescendantAdded` or attribute and property reads, not by reading module state.
- If nothing listens for the value yet, add an attribute hook in the system that owns it. Write it on disk and let Rojo sync it.

Use **`VfxBroadcast.playAt`**, or a `SkillVisuals` primitive that wraps it if one already fits your effect. It sends the effect to every client, and each client draws it.

Don't call `spawnEffect` from the server. It only draws locally, so no player would see the burst. `playOn` attaches an effect to an instance, and `shockwave` is for ring effects. See `docs/agents/vfx-sfx.md:18`.

**Why:** A `.meta.json` file can only change an instance that Rojo is already creating from a sibling file, such as `Ping.luau` or a `Ping/` directory. There's no `Ping` source file in that folder, so `Ping.meta.json` has nothing to attach to. Rojo ignores it and never creates the instance.

**Fix:** Rename the file to `src/shared/Foo/Remotes/Ping.model.json` and keep the same content:

```json
{"className": "RemoteEvent"}
```

A `.model.json` file creates its own instance, and its required `className` key is already there. Make sure `Ping.meta.json` is gone afterwards. Rojo will build `Remotes` as a Folder and put the `Ping` RemoteEvent inside it.

```

```

When you upload a Decal through Open Cloud, the id you get back is the Decal's id, not the id of the image inside it. `rbxassetid://<id>` doesn't resolve for that id, so the label stays blank. The `rbxthumb://` URL asks Roblox's thumbnail service to render the asset, and that does work with the Decal id.

imageLabel.Image = "rbxthumb://type=Asset&id=" .. decalId .. "&w=420&h=420"

To measure render cost, use per-frame counts. The cap, quality level and window focus don't change them:

Code you inject with `execute_luau` gets its own copy of every ModuleScript. When you `require` SpellRegistry, you get a fresh copy that only your snippet uses. The running game keeps its own cached table, so your edit never reaches it.

**How to drive gameplay instead:**
- **Set attributes the game already listens for**, for example on a Player, an arena instance or a part. Game code reacts through `GetAttributeChangedSignal`, so the change lands in the real game.
- **Watch the results through instances.** Hook `DescendantAdded` (or attribute and property signals) on Workspace or the arena, and log what spawns or changes.

If the behaviour you need isn't exposed as an attribute yet, add an attribute hook to the system that owns it, on disk, and let Rojo sync it. Details: `wiki/reference/studio-mcp.md`.

The server should call **`VfxBroadcast.playAt`**, which plays an effect at a world position for every client. If the burst is part of a skill, use the matching `SkillVisuals` primitive, which wraps `VfxBroadcast` and handles the routing.

Server code must never call `spawnEffect` directly, because players only see what their own clients draw (`docs/agents/vfx-sfx.md:18`). For effects attached to an instance, use `playOn`. For ring bursts, use `shockwave`.

**Why:** A `.meta.json` file only changes an instance that Rojo already creates from a sibling file or folder with the same name, such as `Ping.luau` or a `Ping/` folder. Nothing named `Ping` exists, so Rojo has nothing to apply the metadata to and creates nothing. The `className` in it goes unused.

**Fix:** Rename the file to `src/shared/Foo/Remotes/Ping.model.json` and keep the same content:

```json
{"className": "RemoteEvent"}
```

A `.model.json` file creates the instance itself. It must declare `className`, and the file name gives the instance its name (`Ping`). Rojo then turns the `Remotes` folder into a `Folder` containing `Ping`.

If code also adds other children to `Remotes` at runtime, add `Remotes/init.meta.json` with `{"className": "Folder", "ignoreUnknownInstances": true}`.

**How to drive gameplay instead:**
- **Set attributes the game already listens for**, for example on a Player, a character or an arena instance. The game's own scripts react to `GetAttributeChangedSignal`, so the change goes through the real code path.
- **Observe results through the DataModel.** Hook `DescendantAdded` or `AttributeChanged`, or read the console with `get_console_output`. Don't inspect module state.
- **Make lasting data changes on disk** and let Rojo sync them.

Call **`VfxBroadcast.playAt`** with the world position, or a `SkillVisuals` helper that wraps it if one already fits your effect. Server code must never call `spawnEffect` directly. Players only see what their clients draw, so the server sends the effect to every client and each client renders it. `playOn` attaches an effect to an instance, and `shockwave` is the third broadcast option.
